summary: Kickoff-style scoping call to align on POC timeline and milestones for Verdant Energy. Agreed on sample workload size, key success criteria (p95 latency < 300ms for core use case, throughput 30 req/s sustained, quality measured via 500 prompt eval set), and a 6-week POC cadence (kickoff, access/setup, mid-point review with benchmarks, exec readout). Security asked for SOC2 docs and network access details. Action items and dates were captured.
transcript: 00:00 Lena Park: Okay everyone, hi thanks for joining. I think we have ~60 minutes, we'll go through POC timeline and milestones and then lock next steps.
00:12 Priya Menon: Hi all, Priya here. We're excited to get this moving. We're evaluating for a customer-facing recommendation engine and want the POC to show latency and cost numbers.
00:25 Daniel Lee: Daniel — infra. We want to validate both hosted and dedicated options, but priority is proving performance on our workload.

00:35 Marco Diaz: Marco from Redwood SE. We'll propose a benchmark plan that covers latency p50/p95, throughput, and quality against your eval prompts. quick note: sometimes our transcripts say "Redwood Dedicayed" but we mean Redwood Dedicated.
00:48 Sara Gomez: I'm Sara, data science. We'll provide a 500-prompt eval set and a 50GB sample dataset. Main metric is response correctness + hallucination rate.

01:05 Lena Park: Great. High level POC milestones we typically do: kickoff, access & setup, mid-point review with benchmarks, and an exec readout. For a typical scope it's about 4–6 weeks; for Verdant we recommended 6 since you want both hosted and dedicated comparisons.
01:26 Priya Menon: 6 weeks sounds fine. Can you walk through the access/setup steps? We have a VPC and strict egress policy.

01:35 Marco Diaz: Sure. For hosted we need a service account to push test payloads, and for dedicated we'll require a VPN or VPC peering for the private deployment option. There's also key management — Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM, but names sometimes get mangled on notes as K-M-S or H-S-M, apologies.
01:58 Omar Patel: From security: we need SOC2, ISO27001 evidence, network diagrams, and a minimal security checklist. Also need to confirm data residency and retention policies.
02:10 Lena Park: We'll attach the security pack in the follow-up. Action: Lena to send SOC2/ISO docs and the security checklist.

02:20 Daniel Lee: For workload sizing — our peak is about 2k users/day, average concurrent is ~30 requests/s during peak window. Each request runs ~300 tokens on average and 512 max. Does that sound reasonable for the benchmark?

02:40 Marco Diaz: Yes that helps a lot. For the POC benchmark we'll simulate 30 sustained req/s and burst tests to 100 req/s for short windows. We should also test longer contexts since you said 512 max — we'll run runs at 256 and 512 context lengths.

03:02 Sara Gomez: On quality: we want to measure top-1 correctness on the 500-prompt set and track a hallucination score. We'll also check latency at 95th percentile — target is under 300ms for interactive UX.

03:18 Lena Park: Noted — success criteria summary: p95 latency < 300ms for core interactive flow, throughput 30 req/s sustained, quality: >85% top-1 correctness on eval set, and hallucination < 5%. We can capture that in the SOW.
03:35 Priya Menon: Is the p95 target realistic on hosted? We might need dedicated to hit it.

03:42 Marco Diaz: Good question — it depends on model choice and quantization. For example, with an optimized open model on Redwood Dedicated you can often hit lower p95s. On hosted we'll run baseline and then recommend configurations (batching, KV cache, quantization) to meet targets.
04:05 Daniel Lee: We'll want cost estimates — not exact but per-1k tokens and per-hour cluster costs — to compare hosted vs dedicated.
04:14 Lena Park: We'll include rough unit economics in the SOW. For dedicated we show expected token cost reduction with quantization and batching assumptions.
04:28 Sara Gomez: Benchmark plan details? What does Marco need from us to run the tests?

04:33 Marco Diaz: Ideally: a) the 500-prompt eval set, b) a small sample of production logs to emulate routing patterns, c) a staging GCP project or permitted egress endpoint to run load tests. We'll provide the harness and scripts.
04:50 Daniel Lee: We'll provision a staging project and share a service account with limited permissions. Security will vet the network path.
05:02 Omar Patel: Network paths: we need to ensure TLS termination and verify no plaintext logs are stored. We'll review Redwood's logging retention options.
05:15 Lena Park: We'll put that in the security pack. Also note: if you go Private we support customer-managed KMS.
05:25 Priya Menon: Timeline — can you propose exact milestone dates for a 6-week POC starting the week of Apr 6?

05:31 Marco Diaz: Sure, proposed timeline: Kickoff Apr 6, Access & Setup Apr 6–10, Baseline runs and initial tuning Apr 13–17, Mid-point review Apr 20 (share preliminary benchmark results), Additional tuning Apr 21–24, Final runs Apr 27–May 1, Exec readout May 4. That's roughly 4 weeks of active testing with buffers -> 6-week overall window including prep and exec scheduling.
06:05 Priya Menon: That schedule works. Can you make the mid-point review include numbers for latency and cost so stakeholders can decide on continuing to dedicated?
06:16 Marco Diaz: Yes mid-point will include p50/p95 latency, throughput, and a cost estimate extrapolated from the runs. We'll also include suggested quantization profiles and any trade-offs.
06:30 Sara Gomez: On models — which models will you test? We prefer open models but want Redwood's recommendations.

06:37 Marco Diaz: We'll test two main model families: a smaller low-latency variant and a higher-quality variant. We'll label them in notes as Model-A (low-latency) and Model-B (higher quality). We'll also test quantized variants; note that some names might get mistranscribed as "Model A1" etc in notes.
06:55 Daniel Lee: For Dedicated we need an estimate of the required GPU types; we typically prefer A100-class but open to recommendations.

07:03 Marco Diaz: We'll recommend GPU classes in the SOW after initial baseline, but typically A100 or H100 depending on model size and latency targets. We'll include autoscaling and burst policies in the config.
07:20 Omar Patel: Data retention — we need to know how Redwood handles logs and input retention for PII concerns.

07:27 Lena Park: Redwood retains minimal logs for 30 days by default for POC; we can adjust in Private to comply with your retention requirements. We'll include retention options in the security pack.
07:40 Priya Menon: Ok. Let's recap milestones and owners.

07:45 Lena Park: Kickoff Apr 6 (Lena/Marco/Priya), Access & setup Apr 6–10 (Daniel/Omar + Marco), Baseline benchmark Apr 13–17 (Marco + Sara), Mid-point review Apr 20 (Marco + Priya), Final runs Apr 27–May 1 (Marco + Sara), Exec readout May 4 (Lena + Priya).
08:08 Daniel Lee: Any blockers we should flag now? Network approvals and dataset access are the main ones.
08:14 Omar Patel: Also contract SOW and required liability clauses — legal will review once SOW is received.
08:24 Lena Park: We'll send a draft SOW and flag security/legal terms to speed review. Action items captured in notes.
08:35 Sara Gomez: For the benchmark harness, can you include automatic generation of latency percentiles and token counts per response? That helps for cost extrapolation.
08:45 Marco Diaz: Yes we include token accounting and detailed traces per request. We'll also produce per-route latency breakdowns.
08:55 Priya Menon: When do you expect to deliver the benchmark scripts?
09:00 Marco Diaz: By 2026-04-03 I'll share the harness and a runbook.
09:07 Daniel Lee: Great. Anything else about success criteria? I want it captured in the SOW explicitly.

09:12 Lena Park: We'll put the success criteria in the SOW: p95 < 300ms, throughput 30 req/s sustained, quality >85% on eval, hallucination <5%, and cost threshold TBD but we'll include unit cost targets.
09:28 Priya Menon: Sounds good. On reporting, mid-point will have a short slide deck and results spreadsheet.
09:36 Marco Diaz: We'll produce a benchmark spreadsheet and a short runbook with configs and assumptions. We'll also include notes on caching/batching settings used so the numbers are reproducible.

09:50 Lena Park: Ok wrapping up, next steps are in the action items. Lena will send SOW and security pack; Marco will send benchmark harness; Daniel to share staging creds; Sara to finalize eval set; Omar to review security checklist.
10:05 Priya Menon: Thanks everyone, looking forward to kickoff Apr 6. We'll check calendars after the recording.
10:12 Lena Park: Thanks all, meeting adjourned.
end_of_transcript_note: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors and mis-attributed speaker labels common to automated meeting exports.
